newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold down on bearish sentiment over IMF.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold down on bearish sentiment over IMF.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended slightly down on Thursday from the New York close following news that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had enough votes to sell gold, dealers and traders said.
Hong Kong gold opened slightly lower from its New York close on Thursday, sparking a short-lived short-covering spree from Asian players which helped gold edge up during morning trade, dealers said.
Later in the morning, producer selling from Australia put pressure on the market, they said.
"We saw some good liquidation from Australia this morning," said one gold trader at an international bank.
Swiss players bought gold in the afternoon, hedging options positions and pushing the price up slightly, industry sources said.

But bearish sentiment following the IMF news prevailed and gold was dragged down by a weaker silver price, and a lack of immediate support from physical buying left little to buoy the market, traders said.
Physical gold demand has not picked up very much, largely due to the four-day mid-autumn moon festival in China and the Hong Kong holiday on Saturday, a gold source said.
Bullion in the territory ended at US$380.70/381.20 an ounce on Friday against New York's US$380.90/381.40 close on Thursday.
Local gold ended HK$11 lower at HK$3,510 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -5.50 on Friday, up from -6 level on Thursday.
